# List Methods

These methods belong to the default `core` group and are called on list receivers. No method mutates its receiver.

| Entry | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`filter`](#filter) | `T[].filter(f: (item: T, index: int) => unknown) => T[]` | The elements for which f is true, in order. |
| [`map`](#map) | `T[].map(f: (item: T, index: int) => U) => U[]` | f of each element, in order. |
| [`flatMap`](#flatmap) | `T[].flatMap(f: (item: T, index: int) => U[]) => U[]` | The elements of f of each element, in order. |
| [`some`](#some) | `T[].some(f: (item: T, index: int) => unknown) => bool` | Whether f is true for some element; stops at the first. |
| [`every`](#every) | `T[].every(f: (item: T, index: int) => unknown) => bool` | Whether f is true for every element; stops at the first that is not. |
| [`find`](#find) | `T[].find(f: (item: T, index: int) => unknown) => T \| null` | The first element for which f is true, or null. |
| [`count`](#count) | `T[].count(f: (item: T, index: int) => unknown) => int` | How many elements f is true for. |
| [`reduce`](#reduce) | `T[].reduce(f: (acc: A, item: T, index: int) => A, init: A) => A` | The fold of the elements from left to right, starting from init. |
| [`sum`](#sum) | `T[].sum() => T \| int where T: number` | The elements added from left to right, from 0. |
| [`min`](#min) | `T[].min() => T \| null where T: ordered` | The smallest element, or null for an empty list. |
| [`max`](#max) | `T[].max() => T \| null where T: ordered` | The largest element, or null for an empty list. |
| [`sort`](#sort) | `T[].sort() => T[] where T: ordered` | The elements in ascending order, by a stable sort. |
| [`sortBy`](#sortby) | `T[].sortBy(f: (item: T, index: int) => K, order?: "asc" \| "desc") => T[] where K: ordered` | The elements in order of their keys, by a stable sort, ascending or in the direction order gives. |
| [`groupBy`](#groupby) | `T[].groupBy(f: (item: T, index: int) => string) => map<T[]>` | For each distinct key, the elements with that key, in order. |
| [`toMap`](#tomap) | `{key: string, value: T}[].toMap() => map<T>` | The map with each record's value under its key; a later record wins. |
| [`unique`](#unique) | `T[].unique() => T[] where T: ordered` | The first occurrence of each value, in order. |
| [`flat`](#flat) | `U[][].flat() => U[]` | The elements of the inner lists, one level, in order. |
| [`reverse`](#reverse) | `T[].reverse() => T[]` | The elements in reverse order. |
| [`first`](#first) | `T[].first() => T \| null` | The first element, or null for an empty list. |
| [`last`](#last) | `T[].last() => T \| null` | The last element, or null for an empty list. |
| [`slice`](#slice) | `T[].slice(start: int, end?: int) => T[]` | The elements from start up to but not including end. |
| [`join`](#join) | `string[].join(sep: string) => string` | The elements with sep between them. |
| [`findIndex`](#findindex) | `T[].findIndex(f: (item: T, index: int) => unknown) => int \| null` | The index of the first element for which f is true, or null. |
| [`indexOf`](#indexof) | `T[].indexOf(x: T) => int \| null` | The index of the first element equal to x, or null. |
| [`minBy`](#minby) | `T[].minBy(f: (item: T, index: int) => K) => T \| null where K: ordered` | The element whose key is the least; of equal keys, the first. |
| [`maxBy`](#maxby) | `T[].maxBy(f: (item: T, index: int) => K) => T \| null where K: ordered` | The element whose key is the greatest; of equal keys, the first. |
| [`uniqueBy`](#uniqueby) | `T[].uniqueBy(f: (item: T, index: int) => K) => T[] where K: ordered` | The first element with each key, in order. |
| [`indexBy`](#indexby) | `T[].indexBy(f: (item: T, index: int) => string) => map<T>` | Each element under its key; a later element replaces an earlier one. |
| [`countBy`](#countby) | `T[].countBy(f: (item: T, index: int) => string) => map<int>` | For each distinct key, how many elements have it. |

## `filter`

The elements for which f is true, in order.

```text
T[].filter: (f: (item: T, index: int) => unknown) => T[]
```

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Receiver | `T[]` |
| Parameters | `f: (item: T, index: int) => unknown` (callback) |
| Returns | `T[]` |
| Returns null | Never |
| Steps | `2*n` |
| Allocation units | `1 + k` |
| Type checker | Narrows element type using `f` |
| Since | `3.0` |

**Examples**

| Expression | Inputs | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xs.filter(x => x > 1)` | `xs = [3,1,2]` | `[3,2]` (11 steps, 3 units) |
| `[[], [1], [], [2, 3]].filter(x => x)` |  | `[[1],[2,3]]` |
| `xs.filter(x => x > 1)` | `xs = []` | `[]` |
| `xs.filter(x => x != null).sum()` | `xs = [1,null,3]` | `4` |
| `["a", "b", "c"].filter((x, i) => i != 1)` |  | `["a","c"]` |
| `xs.filter(x => x)` | `xs = null` | Fails: `null-operand` |

f of each element, in order.

```text
T[].find: (f: (item: T, index: int) => unknown) => T | null
```

## `reduce`

## `sum`

The elements added from left to right, from 0.

```text
T[].sum: () => T | int where T: number
```

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Receiver | `T[]` |
| Parameters | None |
| Returns | `T \| int` |
| Constraints | `T: number` |
| Returns null | Never |
| Steps | `n` |
| Allocation units | `0` |
| Since | `3.0` |

**Run-time failures**

| Code | Kind | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number-range` (`entry`) | `range` | an addition gives a result out of range or not finite |
| `wrong-kind` (`element`) | `kind` | an element is not a number |

**Examples**

| Expression | Inputs | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xs.sum()` | `xs = [1,2,3]` | `6` (4 steps, 0 units) |
| `xs.sum()` | `xs = []` | `0` |
| `[0.1, 0.2].sum()` |  | `0.30000000000000004` |
| `[1, 2.5].sum()` |  | `3.5` |
| `[9007199254740991, 1, -1].sum()` |  | Fails: `number-range` |
| `xs.sum()` | `xs = [1,"2"]` | Fails: `wrong-kind` |

## `sortBy`

The elements in order of their keys, by a stable sort, ascending or in the direction order gives.

```text
T[].sortBy: (f: (item: T, index: int) => K, order?: "asc" | "desc") => T[] where K: ordered
```

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Receiver | `T[]` |
| Parameters | `f: (item: T, index: int) => K` (callback); `order?: "asc" \| "desc"` (optional) |
| Returns | `T[]` |
| Constraints | `K: ordered` |
| Returns null | Never |
| Steps | `2*n + L*(n + sz(keys))` |
| Allocation units | `1 + n` |
| Since | `3.0` |

**Run-time failures**

| Code | Kind | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wrong-kind` (`unordered`) | `kind` | the keys are not all numbers or all strings |
| `wrong-kind` (`order`) | `kind` | order is not "asc" or "desc" |

**Examples**

| Expression | Inputs | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `xs.sortBy(s => len(s))` | `xs = ["bb","a","cc","d"]` | `["a","d","bb","cc"]` (22 steps, 5 units) |
| `[{n: "b", a: 2}, {n: "a", a: 1}, {n: "c", a: 2}].sortBy(p => p.a).map(p => p.n)` |  | `["a","b","c"]` |
| `xs.sortBy(x => x)` | `xs = []` | `[]` |
| `["😀", "\u{ffff}"].sortBy(s => s)` |  | `["\uffff","😀"]` |
| `[{n: "a", k: 1}, {n: "b", k: 2}, {n: "c", k: 1}].sortBy(p => p.k, "desc").map(p => p.n)` |  | `["b","a","c"]` |
| `["\u{ffff}", "😀"].sortBy(s => s, "desc")` |  | `["😀","\uffff"]` |
| `xs.sortBy(x => x)` | `xs = [1,null]` | Fails: `wrong-kind` |
| `xs.sortBy(x => x, "desc")` | `xs = [1,null]` | Fails: `wrong-kind` — sortBy needs all numbers or all strings, found null |
| `xs.sortBy(x => x, d)` | `xs = [2,1], d = "up"` | Fails: `wrong-kind` — sortBy takes "asc" or "desc", found "up" |
| `[1, 0].sortBy(x => 10 / x)` |  | Fails: `divide-by-zero` |

```text
T[].groupBy: (f: (item: T, index: int) => string) => map<T[]>
```

| Field | Value |

## `toMap`

The map with each record's value under its key; a later record wins.

```text
{key: string, value: T}[].toMap: () => map<T>
```

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Receiver | `{key: string, value: T}[]` |
| Parameters | None |
| Returns | `map<T>` |
| Returns null | Never |
| Steps | `n + sz(keys)` |
| Allocation units | `1 + 2*n` |
| Since | `3.0` |

**Run-time failures**

| Code | Kind | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wrong-kind` (`element`) | `kind` | an element is not a map |
| `wrong-kind` (`key`) | `kind` | the key field of an element is not a string |
| `missing-field` (`field`) | `field` | an element has no key named key or value |

**Examples**

| Expression | Inputs | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[{key: "a", value: 1}, {key: "b", value: 2}].toMap()` |  | `{"a":1,"b":2}` |

| `es.toMap()` | `es = []` | `{}` |
| `es.toMap()` | `es = [{"key":"a"}]` | Fails: `missing-field` |
| `es.toMap()` | `es = [{"key":"a","value":1},{"key":1,"value":2}]` | Fails: `wrong-kind` |
